source.title: Retrieval Capabilities of Large Language Models Scale with Pretraining FLOPs
source.authors: J. Portes; Connor Jennings; Erica Ji Yuen; Sasha Doubov; Michael Carbin

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream retrieval performance across model sizes and pretraining durations, using BEIR retrieval scores rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss.
record.gate_note: The study reports retrieval-scaling results and an ICL–retrieval correlation. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit pretraining loss power laws, test extrapolation of such fits, or find compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study measures zero-shot BEIR retrieval (nDCG@10) of MPT decoders from 125M to 7B parameters and 3B to 2T pretraining tokens, after the same MS MARCO fine-tune. That is a downstream result on how performance changes with model size, tokens and FLOPs, which bears directly on V6 in a new setting (decoder-based dense retrieval). No pretraining loss is measured or fitted, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that zero-shot BEIR retrieval after minimal MS MARCO fine-tuning improves predictably with model size, pretraining duration and estimated FLOPs, and is best summarised by accuracy-versus-FLOPs curves. Small models trained longer can match larger models trained on less data. ICL scores correlate strongly with retrieval scores. They explicitly do not derive formal scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: Measures downstream BEIR retrieval after contrastive MS MARCO fine-tuning rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss; reports empirical trends rather than fitted loss laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Retrieval trends differ by BEIR task: ArguAna essentially plateaus, and Touche2020 is identified as an exception. The study also notes that MPT-3B is better than MPT-125M on ICL tasks even where retrieval scores can match.

fits_no_version.finding: Across pretrained checkpoints, ICL Gauntlet scores are strongly correlated with BEIR scores after contrastive fine-tuning. No correlation coefficient is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained checkpoints with higher ICL scores yield better retrievers after contrastive fine-tuning.

record.problems: The authors do not derive formal scaling laws. Score values are presented in figures rather than stated in the text; no uncertainty estimates are reported. All checkpoints use the same fine-tuning hyperparameters without hyperparameter sweeps, and fine-tuning/evaluation use a maximum sequence length of 128 tokens. ArguAna plateaus and Touche2020 is an exception whose results are not shown.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately reported result rows left out. Figure 2 task-level trends are described as generally similar, but separate task scores are not given in text; the expressly noted exceptions are recorded in R17–R18.

untested.parts: Whether downstream retrieval tracks pretraining loss (loss is never measured). No fitted law and no extrapolation from small to large runs, so predictability is shown only as a monotone trend. No other downstream task families beyond BEIR retrieval.

missing.what: Two MPT-7B checkpoints (2T tokens, 285 tokens per parameter) have slightly higher average nDCG@10 than MPT-3B at 500 tokens per parameter. This extends the size sweep to 7B.
Per-task BEIR scaling: tasks other than ArguAna and Touche2020 follow the Figure 1 trends. Llama 2 7B and Mistral 7B, fine-tuned with the same recipe, are plotted on some tasks.

record.verdict_notes: The tranche is changed from T2 to T3: the study is a new downstream setting (retrieval), not a different method for loss scaling. The study uses a single fixed fine-tuning recipe (128-token sequences, no hyperparameter sweeps), which the authors call lower bounds. It reports no uncertainty. FLOPs use the 6ND approximation, and Mistral's FLOPs are assumed. The Section 3.5 equivalence (R4 vs R12, 125M at 1.5T tokens matching 1B at 25.2B) is consistent with performance tracking compute rather than size alone.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures downstream retrieval scores, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss.
It does not fit small-run pretraining-loss curves or compare their predictions with larger runs.
It does not find loss-minimising parameter/token allocations at fixed compute.
It does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns text retrieval after MS MARCO fine-tuning; it does not test other modalities or the listed training regimes.
Tests retrieval performance after the same MS MARCO fine-tuning recipe, not downstream tasks generally or scaling against pretraining loss.
It does not vary fitting methods or parameters, compare fitted exponents, or test loss-curve bending or compute-optimal allocation.

rows.operation_detail: Compared average BEIR retrieval performance across model sizes at a token-per-parameter ratio of 20.

rows.check: Each of R1–R16 is one point on a plotted curve, with values only in Figure 1. 'Observed' means the authors describe a smooth or steady increase across the sweep, not a separately reported per-checkpoint effect. The rows' baselines are effectively the neighbouring checkpoints.

rows.subject: MPT checkpoints across sizes and pretraining durations
rows.stage_stated: Pretrained checkpoints; then fine-tuned for one epoch on 500,000 MS MARCO samples
rows.operation_detail: Measured retrieval performance on the ArguAna task across increasing pretraining FLOPs.
rows.value: figure only; text says performance essentially plateaus
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the reported scaling sweep; the authors identify ArguAna as an exception to the trends on other tasks.
rows.check: The text says ArguAna performance 'essentially plateaus despite increasing FLOPs'. That means no scaling gain, which is absent, not partial.

rows.operation_detail: Reported retrieval performance as an exception to the otherwise similar task-level scaling trends.
rows.value: not stated; identified as an exception, with results not shown
rows.note: The paper identifies Touche2020 as a notable exception but does not describe the direction or magnitude of its result.
rows.check: Touche2020 is named as an exception but its results are 'not shown'. The direction and size of the result cannot be read, so the state cannot be partial.

rows.subject: Pretrained MPT checkpoints
rows.stage_stated: Pretrained; retrieval models fine-tuned on MS MARCO
rows.operation_detail: Compared BEIR retrieval scores with In-Context Learning scores from the MosaicML Evaluation Gauntlet.
rows.measure: Association between BEIR retrieval scores and ICL scores
rows.value: strongly correlated; numerical correlation not stated
rows.note: The authors say that almost without exception, checkpoints with higher ICL scores also have higher retrieval scores.
rows.check: The row correlates ICL score with retrieval score. ICL is neither pretraining loss nor a scale variable, so it does not measure V6 as stated. It is correctly kept under fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: Average BEIR nDCG@10 across the MPT size sweep (125M–3B at 20 tokens per parameter) and the training-duration sweeps (125M up to 10,000 tokens per parameter; 3B up to 500)
relationships.reason: The authors report a smooth increase with model size and a steady, non-plateauing increase with tokens and FLOPs (R1–R16). MPT-7B at 2T tokens scores slightly above MPT-3B (text, Section 3.4). Values appear in figures only.
relationships.display_finding: Average BEIR nDCG@10 increased smoothly with model size and without plateauing as tokens and FLOPs increased, with MPT-7B at 2T tokens slightly exceeding MPT-3B.

relationships.reason: ArguAna performance essentially plateaus despite increasing FLOPs, so scaling does not improve this task under the uninstructed recipe (R17).
relationships.display_finding: Performance remained essentially flat as pretraining FLOPs increased.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
